text:
Minnesota spent the first period doing most of the damage and went into the second tied 2-2. Kirill Kaprizov scored both goals, the second one 44 seconds after Mark Scheifele put Winnipeg ahead with 6 minutes left in the period, and the Wild had out-chanced the Jets 1.53 to 0.82 in expected goals. Cole Perfetti's tip-in at 1:50 was a 4 percent chance that went in anyway.

Then the game turned. Winnipeg produced 1.58 expected goals in the second to Minnesota's 0.58, and Perfetti scored his second of the night on a power play at 16:36 to make it 3-2. Kyle Connor added a wrist shot early in the third, and Cole Koepke closed it out at 14:42. The Wild generated 0.38 expected goals in the third, and they never threatened to get back into it.

The final was 5-2, but the play was closer than that. Winnipeg finished with 2.82 expected goals to Minnesota's 2.49, and the Jets would win about 56 percent of simulated replays of every shot. Calvin Pickard made the difference look larger: he allowed 5 goals on 2.82 expected, 2.18 worse than a typical goalie would have managed, while Stuart Skinner stopped 19 of 21 and finished slightly ahead of expectation. Scheifele's three points and Neal Pionk's two assists earned them first and third star, with Perfetti's pair of goals between them.
